{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVMWpgs8AAAABZarz1Q", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BnW-xzhDCAko", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BnW-x", "number": 39, "title": "Keep classic SCC audio continuous when its registers or cartridge slot are hidden", "body": "## Problem

Programmed classic K051649 SCC voices become silent whenever software disables the 9800h–9FFFh register overlay or maps another slot into that page. `Machine::step` derives an `audible` flag from memory visibility, and `Psg::tick_with_scc` suppresses the SCC contribution while that flag is false. Oscillators already keep advancing.

Register accessibility should control CPU reads and writes; it should not mute an installed, programmed sound chip. The current behavior can interrupt music during ordinary bank and slot changes. No commercial-game failure was directly observed.

## Expected outcome

Classic SCC playback and phase continue across overlay and slot changes on MSX1/MSX2. Hidden accesses cannot change SCC registers. Explicit channel/volume controls and existing reset, ejection and replacement behavior remain effective.

## Context

Baseline: `ae711ff47e0ebd0aeb2afdf93326d7e0a71eee95`, matching inspected GitHub main and the clean evaluation checkout. Relevant files are `crates/msx-core/src/{lib,psg,cartridge,scc}.rs`, `crates/msx-core/tests/scc.rs`, `crates/msx-core/src/psg/tests.rs`, `crates/msx-core/src/firmware/scc_fixture.rs`, `tests/scc.spec.js`, and SCC documentation/help.

This deliberately corrects the hidden-window silence requirement from closed [Issue #23](https://github.com/takahirox/msx-rust/issues/23), implemented by [PR #24](https://github.com/takahirox/msx-rust/pull/24). Existing native and browser tests enforce that incorrect expectation. [Inspected PR-head CI](https://github.com/takahirox/msx-rust/actions/runs/39975457798) reports 147 Rust and 88 browser tests passing, including the native overlay-silence test. Those results establish regression evidence, not hardware correctness. This planning task ran no tests.

Behavioral references:

- Pinned openMSX [mapper decoding](https://github.com/openMSX/openMSX/blob/26e1e4945df406e250a05122889f88d40edd828b/src/memory/RomKonamiSCC.cc) changes register visibility without muting channels; its [SCC synthesis](https://github.com/openMSX/openMSX/blob/26e1e4945df406e250a05122889f88d40edd828b/src/sound/SCC.cc) generates sound independently of that visibility.
- The [libmsx SCC interface and tone example](https://mori0091.github.io/libmsx/group__SCC__DEVICE.html) distinguish register exposure from channel controls and restore the previous slot before hiding the programmed chip.

Continuity is inferred from these inspected upstream implementations/documentation; no new physical measurement establishes it. The Japanese hardware investigation remained text-corrupted, and the NGS reference returned 403. These limitations do not prevent the focused correction. Delayed DAC updates, SCC-I, synthesis redesign and instruction bus-phase scheduling remain separate work.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Separate installed SCC audio generation from overlay/slot accessibility. Preserve existing selected-slot register decoding, bank masks, mirrors, ROM visibility and hidden-write isolation. Avoid unnecessary abstractions or public Wasm ABI changes.
- [ ] Replace hidden-silence assertions with independently authored native PCM regressions on both models. Cover overlay disabling, slot hiding, combined transitions and restoration, including hidden waveform, frequency, volume and enable writes that must not reach SCC. Check audio during hidden intervals, not only after restoration.
- [ ] Verify sample values, pitch and uninterrupted phase against independently calculated expectations and an equal-elapsed-cycle visible control. Include intervals crossing sample/frame boundaries and irregular tick partitions. For example, the existing ±120 waveform at volume 15 and period 253 yields +0.056/−0.0565 samples under the retained gain and repeats every `32 × 254` CPU cycles. Preserve five-voice/shared-wave and simultaneous PSG coverage.
- [ ] Exercise genuine Z80 memory and slot-port writes using an original redistributable probe. Reuse or extend the existing SCC fixture and real compiled Wasm/browser tests on both models, explicit/Auto mapping and both hosting roots. Verify continuity in captured PCM and fresh scheduled Web Audio buffers; account for queued audio and frame gaps. Do not substitute a synthesizer or require a production debug API.
- [ ] Retain explicit register-controlled silence, browser mute/resume and pause behavior, reset/eject/replacement silence, and transactional failed-import preservation. Preserve existing PSG envelope timing, disk, SRAM, firmware, mapper, ownership and provenance behavior through the applicable regression suites.
- [ ] Update the fixture, README, SCC documentation and affected help/comments so hiding registers is no longer described as muting audio. Ensure fixture controls can still explicitly silence voices, including after hidden intervals. Preserve licensing and distinguish hardware support from unobserved commercial compatibility.
- [ ] The Coordinator runs and reports `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `./scripts/build.sh`, `node scripts/check-dist.mjs`, and `npm test`, with README-documented dependency setup as needed. Demonstrate the new continuity regression fails on the baseline. Complete repository-required review and resolve blocking findings before merge; distinguish passed, failed, skipped and unperformed checks.

## Optional validation

Run the original probe in a pinned openMSX configuration using lawfully available firmware and compare visibility transitions and PCM phase. Record configuration and limitations. This is supplementary and has not been performed here.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
